sanskrit: darśanārthaṃ tu vaidehyāḥ sarvataḥ kapiyūthapāḥ vyādiṣṭāḥ kapirājena yathoktaṃ jagmur añjasā
english: For the sake of finding Vaidehī, the leaders of the monkey troops, dispatched by the monkey-king as instructed, set forth swiftly in all directions.

sanskrit: sarāṃsi saritaḥ kakṣān ākāśaṃ nagarāṇi ca nadīdurgāṃs tathā śailān vicinvanti samantataḥ
english: They searched all around through lakes, rivers, thickets, the sky, and cities, through river-fastnesses and mountains on every side.

sanskrit: sugrīveṇa samākhyātān sarve vānarayūthapāḥ pradeśān pravicinvanti saśailavanakānanān
english: All the leaders of the monkey troops thoroughly searched the regions named by Sugrīva, along with their mountains, forests, and woodlands.

sanskrit: vicintya divasaṃ sarve sītādhigamane dhṛtāḥ samāyānti sma medinyāṃ niśākāleśu vānarāḥ
english: Having searched throughout the day, all the monkeys, resolute in finding Sītā, would return to the earth when night came.

sanskrit: sarvartukāṃś ca deśeṣu vānarāḥ saphalān drumān āsādya rajanīṃ śayyāṃ cakruḥ sarveṣv ahaḥsu te
english: In regions bearing fruit in every season, the monkeys would come to fruit-laden trees and make their nightly resting places, day after day.

sanskrit: tad ahaḥ prathamaṃ kṛtvā māse prasravaṇaṃ gatāḥ kapirājena saṃgamya nirāśāḥ kapiyūthapāḥ
english: Having completed the first appointed day, the leaders of the monkey troops returned to Prasravaṇa at the end of the month and met with the monkey-king, having found nothing.

sanskrit: vicitya tu diśaṃ pūrvāṃ yathoktāṃ sacivaiḥ saha adṛṣṭvā vinataḥ sītām ājagāma mahābalaḥ
english: Having searched the eastern direction as instructed, along with his ministers, mighty Vinatā returned without having seen Sītā.

sanskrit: uttarāṃ tu diśaṃ sarvāṃ vicitya sa mahākapiḥ āgataḥ saha sainyena vīraḥ śatabalis tadā
english: And that great monkey, the valiant Śatabali, having searched the entire northern direction, returned together with his army.

sanskrit: suṣeṇaḥ paścimām āśāṃ vicitya saha vānaraiḥ sametya māse saṃpūrṇe sugrīvam upacakrame
english: Suṣeṇa, having searched the western quarter together with the monkeys, approached Sugrīva when the full month was spent.

sanskrit: taṃ prasravaṇapṛṣṭhasthaṃ samāsādyābhivādya ca āsīnaṃ saha rāmeṇa sugrīvam idam abruvan
english: Approaching Sugrīva, who was seated on the summit of Prasravaṇa together with Rāma, they saluted him and spoke these words.

sanskrit: vicitāḥ parvatāḥ sarve vanāni nagarāṇi ca nimnagāḥ sāgarāntāś ca sarve janapadās tathā
english: "All the mountains have been searched, and all the forests and cities, the rivers reaching to the ocean, and all the inhabited lands.

sanskrit: guhāś ca vicitāḥ sarvā yās tvayā parikīrtitāḥ vicitāś ca mahāgulmā latāvitatasaṃtatāḥ
english: All the caves named by you have been searched, and the great thickets overgrown and interlaced with creepers have been searched as well.

sanskrit: gahaneṣu ca deśeṣu durgeṣu viṣameṣu ca sattvāny atipramāṇāni vicitāni hatāni ca ye caiva gahanā deśā vicitās te punaḥ punaḥ
english: In dense, inaccessible, and rugged regions, creatures of immense size have been searched out and slain; and those dense places have been searched again and again.

sanskrit: udārasattvābhijano mahātmā sa maithilīṃ drakṣyati vānarendraḥ diśaṃ tu yām eva gatā tu sītā tām āsthito vāyusuto hanūmān
english: That great-souled foremost of monkeys, born of noble spirit, will behold Maithilī; for Hanūmān, son of the Wind, has taken the very direction in which Sītā went."

sanskrit: sahatārāṅgadābhyāṃ tu gatvā sa hanumān kapiḥ sugrīveṇa yathoddiṣṭaṃ taṃ deśam upacakrame
english: Then that monkey Hanūmān, going together with Tārā and Aṅgada, approached the region indicated by Sugrīva.

sanskrit: sa tu dūram upāgamya sarvais taiḥ kapisattamaiḥ vicinoti sma vindhyasya guhāś ca gahanāni ca
english: Having gone far, together with all those best of monkeys, he searched the caves and dense forests of the Vindhya range.

sanskrit: parvatāgrān nadīdurgān sarāṃsi vipulān drumān vṛkṣaṣaṇḍāṃś ca vividhān parvatān ghanapādapān
english: The summits of mountains, river-fastnesses, lakes, vast trees, diverse groves of trees, and mountains thick with foliage—

sanskrit: anveṣamāṇās te sarve vānarāḥ sarvato diśam na sītāṃ dadṛśur vīrā maithilīṃ janakātmajām
english: —all those valiant monkeys, searching in every direction, did not find Sītā, the daughter of Janaka, Maithilī.

sanskrit: te bhakṣayanto mūlāni phalāni vividhāni ca anveṣamāṇā durdharṣā nyavasaṃs tatra tatra ha sa tu deśo duranveṣo guhāgahanavān mahān
english: Eating roots and various fruits as they searched, those formidable ones dwelt here and there; for that region was vast, hard to search, full of caves and dense forest.

sanskrit: tyaktvā tu taṃ tadā deśaṃ sarve vai hariyūthapāḥ deśam anyaṃ durādharṣaṃ viviśuś cākutobhayāḥ
english: Leaving that region then, all the leaders of the monkey troops, fearless and undaunted, entered another forbidding land.

sanskrit: yatra vandhyaphalā vṛkṣā vipuṣpāḥ parṇavarjitāḥ nistoyāḥ sarito yatra mūlaṃ yatra sudurlabham
english: Where the trees bore no fruit, were flowerless and stripped of leaves; where the rivers were waterless, and roots were extremely scarce—

sanskrit: na santi mahiṣā yatra na mṛgā na ca hastinaḥ śārdūlāḥ pakṣiṇo vāpi ye cānye vanagocarāḥ
english: —where there were no buffaloes, no deer, no elephants, no tigers, no birds, nor any other forest-dwelling creatures—

sanskrit: snigdhapatrāḥ sthale yatra padminyaḥ phullapaṅkajāḥ prekṣaṇīyāḥ sugandhāś ca bhramaraiś cāpi varjitāḥ
english: —where on dry land there were lotus-pools with gleaming, full-blown lotuses, beautiful and fragrant, yet forsaken even by bees—

sanskrit: kaṇḍur nāma mahābhāgaḥ satyavādī tapodhanaḥ maharṣiḥ paramāmarṣī niyamair duṣpradharṣaṇaḥ
english: —there lived a great sage named Kaṇḍu, most glorious, truth-speaking, rich in austerities, utterly intolerant, and unapproachable through his self-discipline—

sanskrit: tasya tasmin vane putro bālako daśavārṣikaḥ pranaṣṭo jīvitāntāya kruddhas tatra mahāmuniḥ
english: —whose son, a boy of ten years, was lost to death in that very forest; the great sage, enraged, cursed that place—

sanskrit: tena dharmātmanā śaptaṃ kṛtsnaṃ tatra mahad vanam aśaraṇyaṃ durādharṣaṃ mṛgapakṣivivarjitam
english: —by that righteous-souled one the entire great forest was cursed: desolate, forbidding, devoid of beasts and birds.

sanskrit: tasya te kānanāntāṃs tu girīṇāṃ kandarāṇi ca prabhavāni nadīnāṃca vicinvanti samāhitāḥ
english: The borders of that forest, the ravines of the mountains, and the headwaters of rivers they searched with careful attention.

sanskrit: tatra cāpi mahātmāno nāpaśyañ janakātmajām hartāraṃ rāvaṇaṃ vāpi sugrīvapriyakāriṇaḥ
english: And there too those great-souled ones, devoted to Sugrīva's good, did not see the daughter of Janaka, nor Rāvaṇa, her abductor.

sanskrit: te praviśya tu taṃ bhīmaṃ latāgulmasamāvṛtam dadṛśuḥ krūrakarmāṇam asuraṃ suranirbhayam
english: Entering that terrible region overgrown with creepers and thickets, they saw a demon of cruel deeds, fearless even of the gods.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā vanarā ghoraṃ sthitaṃ śailam ivāparam gāḍhaṃ parihitāḥ sarve dṛṣṭvā taṃ parvatopamam
english: Seeing that terrible one standing there like another mountain, all the monkeys drew closely together upon beholding that mountain-like figure.

sanskrit: so 'pi tān vānarān sarvān naṣṭāḥ sthety abravīd balī abhyadhāvata saṃkruddho muṣṭim udyamya saṃhitam
english: That powerful one said to all the monkeys, "You are finished!" and, raising his clenched fist, charged at them in great fury.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ sahasā vāliputro 'ṅgadas tadā rāvaṇo 'yam iti jñātvā talenābhijaghāna ha
english: As he rushed forward, Aṅgada, son of Vālin, recognizing him as Rāvaṇa, struck him on the spot with the flat of his palm.

sanskrit: sa vāliputrābhihato vaktrāc choṇitam udvaman asuro nyapatad bhūmau paryasta iva parvataḥ
english: Struck by the son of Vālin and vomiting blood from his mouth, that demon fell to the ground like a mountain toppled over.

sanskrit: te tu tasmin nirucchvāse vānarā jitakāśinaḥ vyacinvan prāyaśas tatra sarvaṃ tad girigahvaram
english: While he lay breathless, the monkeys, exulting in victory, searched most of that mountain-gorge region all around.

sanskrit: vicitaṃ tu tataḥ kṛtvā sarve te kānanaṃ punaḥ anyadevāparaṃ ghoraṃ viviśur girigahvaram
english: Having searched that forest, all of them then entered yet another terrible mountain-cavern.

sanskrit: te vicintya punaḥ khinnā viniṣpatya samāgatāḥ ekānte vṛkṣamūle tu niṣedur dīnamānasāḥ
english: Searching again, exhausted, they leapt out and came together, sitting down at the foot of a solitary tree with downcast hearts.

sanskrit: athāṅgadas tadā sarvān vānarān idam abravīt pariśrānto mahāprājñaḥ samāśvāsya śanair vacaḥ
english: Then Aṅgada, most wise, exhausted, gently composing himself, spoke these words to all the monkeys.

sanskrit: vanāni girayo nadyo durgāṇi gahanāni ca daryo giriguhāś caiva vicitā naḥ samantataḥ
english: "Forests, mountains, rivers, fastnesses, dense thickets, cliffs, and mountain-caves — all have been searched by us on every side.

sanskrit: tatra tatra sahāsmābhir jānakī na ca dṛśyate tad vā rakṣo hṛtā yena sītā surasutopamā
english: Everywhere, even among us, Jānakī cannot be seen — Sītā, equal to the daughter of the gods, carried off by some demon.

sanskrit: kālaś ca no mahān yātaḥ sugrīvaś cograśāsanaḥ tasmād bhavantaḥ sahitā vicinvantu samantataḥ
english: A great time has already passed for us, and Sugrīva is fierce in his commands; therefore let all of you together continue to search on every side.

sanskrit: vihāya tandrīṃ śokaṃ ca nidrāṃ caiva samutthitām vicinudhvaṃ yathā sītāṃ paśyāmo janakātmajām
english: Abandoning sloth, grief, and the sleep that has come upon you, search so that we may find Sītā, the daughter of Janaka.

sanskrit: anirvedaṃ ca dākṣyaṃ ca manasaś cāparājayam kāryasiddhikarāṇy āhus tasmād etad bravīmy aham
english: Perseverance, skill, and the unconquered spirit of the mind — these are said to bring success in one's tasks; therefore I say this to you.

sanskrit: adyāpīdaṃ vanaṃ durgaṃ vicinvantu vanaukasaḥ khedaṃ tyaktvā punaḥ sarvaṃ vanam etad vicīyatām
english: Even today let the forest-dwellers search this inaccessible forest; abandoning weariness, let this entire forest be searched once more.

sanskrit: avaśyaṃ kriyamāṇasya dṛśyate karmaṇaḥ phalam alaṃ nirvedam āgamya na hi no malinaṃ kṣamam
english: The fruit of an action diligently performed is surely seen; enough of despondency — for dejection is not fitting for us.

sanskrit: sugrīvaḥ krodhano rājā tīkṣṇadaṇḍaś ca vānarāḥ bhetavyaṃ tasya satataṃ rāmasya ca mahātmanaḥ
english: Sugrīva, O monkeys, is a wrathful king, swift to punish; one must always be wary of him, and of the great-souled Rāma as well.

sanskrit: hitārtham etad uktaṃ vaḥ kriyatāṃ yadi rocate ucyatāṃ vā kṣamaṃ yan naḥ sarveṣām eva vānarāḥ
english: This has been said for your own good; act on it if it pleases you, or else say, O monkeys, what is proper for all of us together."

sanskrit: aṅgadasya vacaḥ śrutvā vacanaṃ gandhamādanaḥ uvācāvyaktayā vācā pipāsā śramakhinnayā
english: Having heard Aṅgada's words, Gandhamādana spoke in a faint voice, weakened by thirst and fatigue.

sanskrit: sadṛśaṃ khalu vo vākyam aṅgado yad uvāca ha hitaṃ caivānukūlaṃ ca kriyatām asya bhāṣitam
english: "Indeed, what Aṅgada has said is worthy of you — it is both beneficial and agreeable; let what he has said be done."

sanskrit: punar mārgāmahe śailān kandarāṃś ca darīs tathā kānanāni ca śūnyāni giriprasravaṇāni ca
english: "Let us search once more: mountains, ravines, and cliffs as well, the empty woodlands and the mountain-springs."

sanskrit: yathoddiṣṭhāni sarvāṇi sugrīveṇa mahātmanā vicinvantu vanaṃ sarve giridurgāṇi sarvaśaḥ
english: "Let all search everywhere through the forest and the mountain-fastnesses, exactly as all of them were indicated by great-souled Sugrīva."

sanskrit: tataḥ samutthāya punar vānarās te mahābalāḥ vindhyakānanasaṃkīrṇāṃ vicerur dakṣiṇāṃ diśam
english: Then those mighty monkeys rose up again and roamed the southern direction, which was interspersed with Vindhya forests.

sanskrit: te śāradābhrapratimaṃ śrīmadrajataparvatam śṛṅgavantaṃ darīvantam adhiruhya ca vānarāḥ
english: Those monkeys climbed the glorious Silver Mountain, resembling an autumn cloud, full of peaks and caves.

sanskrit: tatra lodhravanaṃ ramyaṃ saptaparṇavanāni ca vicinvanto harivarāḥ sītādarśanakāṅkṣiṇaḥ
english: There the best of monkeys, eager to behold Sītā, searched through the charming lodhra-forests and the saptaparṇa-groves.

sanskrit: tasyāgram adhirūḍhās te śrāntā vipulavikramāḥ na paśyanti sma vaidehīṃ rāmasya mahiṣīṃ priyām
english: Climbing to its summit, those great-striding ones, though exhausted, did not see Vaidehī, the beloved queen of Rāma.

sanskrit: te tu dṛṣṭigataṃ kṛtvā taṃ śailaṃ bahukandaram avārohanta harayo vīkṣamāṇāḥ samantataḥ
english: Having surveyed that mountain of many caverns to the full extent of their sight, the monkeys descended, looking all around.

sanskrit: avaruhya tato bhūmiṃ śrāntā vigatacetasaḥ sthitvā muhūrtaṃ tatrātha vṛkṣamūlam upāśritāḥ
english: Having descended to the ground, exhausted and dispirited, they rested for a moment and then took shelter at the foot of a tree.

sanskrit: te muhūrtaṃ samāśvastāḥ kiṃ cid bhagnapariśramāḥ punar evodyatāḥ kṛtsnāṃ mārgituṃ dakṣiṇāṃ diśam
english: Having recovered for a moment, somewhat relieved of exhaustion, they rose once more, determined to search the entire southern direction.

sanskrit: hanumatpramukhās te tu prasthitāḥ plavagarṣabhāḥ vindhyam evāditas tāvad vicerus te samantataḥ
english: Those best of leaping monkeys, with Hanūmān at their head, set forth and ranged all around the Vindhya from its very beginning.
